column1: # title: Table 9 Alternating-Current (ac)Resistance and Reactance for 600-Volt Cables
# note: 1. These values are based on the following constants: UL-Type RHH wires with Class B stranding
column2: in cradled configuration. Wire conductivities are 100 percent IACS copper and 61 percent IACS aluminum
column3: and aluminum conduit is 45 percent IACS. Capacitive reactance is ignored
column4: since it is negligible at these voltages. These resistance values are valid only at 75°C (167°F) and for the parameters as given
column5: but are representative for 600-volt wire types operating at 60 Hz.

column1: # note: 2. Effective Z is defined as R cos(θ) + X sin(θ)
column2: where θ is the power factor angle of the circuit. Multiplying current by effective impedance gives a good approximation for line-to-neutral voltage drop. Effective impedance values shown in this table are valid only at 0.85 power factor. For another circuit power factor (PF)
column3: effective impedance (Ze) can be calculated from R and XL values given in this table as follows: Ze = R × PF + XL sin[arccos(PF)].
